proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a successful published run satisfying the two support hypotheses. By \(\textnormal{lem:published-trace-scheduling}\), the input-determined compiler follows a dependency-topological simulation of that run, never enters a residual state before its successful terminal call, and then presents the same reduced circuit \(F_H=P_H/D_H\) to the projection verifier. Its exact accumulated identity is
\[
 D_H\,t_{a,H}^N-P_H(o_H^N)=0\pmod{\mathcal J}.
\tag{18}
\]
Every factor of \(D_H\) is a context normalizer, reachable fixing margin, or reduced elimination denominator paired with the corresponding ledger factorization. The hypothesis that the published run uses only contexts in \(H\) ensures that every initial normalizer is
\[
 p_H(S=s)=
 \sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v,s),
 \qquad s\in H.
\tag{19}
\]
By \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\), (19) is a nonempty sum of strictly positive cells. The inductive certificates in \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\), together with \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\), give
\[
 d_{H,r}\{O_H(\theta)\}>0
 \quad\text{for every registered }r
 \quad\text{and every }\theta\in\Theta_H.
\tag{20}
\]
The definition of the branch domain and (20) imply
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{21}
\]

On this domain \(D_H>0\), so division in (18) is legitimate and yields
\[
 t_{a,H}^N(\eta)
 =F_H\{O_H^N(\eta)\}
 \qquad(\eta\in\mathcal I_H).
\tag{22}
\]
For \(\theta\in\Theta_H\), put \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\). The normalization equivalence theorem gives
\[
 O_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=O_H(\theta),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta).
\tag{23}
\]
Substitution of (23) into (22) proves
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)
 \qquad(\theta\in\Theta_H).
\tag{24}
\]
Finally, the scheduling lemma proves operation-by-operation equality, modulo the stored gate and retained-image equations, of the normalized labelled kernels and the published kernels after gate reinsertion. Equations (19)--(20) identify their required positive margins as well. This is the asserted algebraic preservation on the original expansion, and no selector value outside \(H\) has been introduced.

Let \(q\) be a kernel induced by a hidden-variable recursive structural causal model and let \(\pi_1\) and \(\pi_2\) be valid fixing sequences for the same set of random vertices in the same CADMG. Then
\[
 \phi_{\pi_1}(q;G)=\phi_{\pi_2}(q;G).
\]

added_lemmas.statement: For every nonterminal normalized state refreshed by \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\), exactly one of the following cases is selected: an actually present supported-context selector occurrence; a nonempty set of nonancestors of the local outcome; a split into at least two explicitly computed districts; a canonically least reachable vertex with an inductively constructed positive-margin certificate; or a residual-ready state. In each of the first four cases the selected token is currently eligible, its exact local identity and positivity certificate are constructible by finite arithmetic, and the corresponding transition exists. After refreshing the successor agenda, \(\mu_H\) strictly decreases. Hence the fixed input-determined machine cannot stop before reaching a residual-ready state.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a normalized nonterminal state \(\zeta\). By \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\), every vertex alphabet, context list, graph, kernel circuit, and response table in \(\zeta\) is finite. Membership in \(H\), occurrence of a stored gate, ancestor and district computation, and the condition
\[
 \operatorname{dis}_{G_\zeta}(W)\cap
 \operatorname{de}_{G_\zeta}(W)=\{W\}
\tag{7}
\]
are therefore decidable by finite enumeration. Consequently \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\) executes one and only one branch of its ordered case definition. This already proves exhaustivity and mutual exclusivity of the five cases. We prove eligibility and progress in the four nonresidual cases.

Suppose first that \(\mathsf G(\zeta)\neq\varnothing\). Every member \((s,X,r,x_s)\) of this list is, by construction, an occurrence actually present in a labelled kernel and has \(s\in H\). At this occurrence the stored zero--one selector equation gives
\[
 X=x_s,
 \qquad
 \mathbf 1\{X=x\}=\mathbf 1\{x_s=x\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus substitution of \(x_s\) in its children is an exact polynomial identity modulo the gate-copy equations in \(\mathcal J\). The only initialization divisor is
\[
 q(S=s)=
 \sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}q(v,s)>0.
\tag{9}
\]
The sum is nonempty because \(s\in H\), and every summand indexed by an admissible cell is positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\). Hence the least selector token satisfies every eligibility clause of \(\textnormal{def:selector-transition}\). Rewriting one stored multiplexer cannot create another multiplexer occurrence, so the refreshed value of \(|\Sigma|\) is smaller by one. The first coordinate \(|R|\) is unchanged; therefore the corrected lexicographic measure, whose selector coordinate precedes both elimination and fixing work, decreases.

Now suppose \(\mathsf G(\zeta)=\varnothing\) and \(Z_\zeta\neq\varnothing\). By definition,
\[
 \varnothing\neq Z_\zeta
 \subseteq R_\zeta\setminus\operatorname{an}_{G_\zeta}(Y_\zeta).
\tag{10}
\]
The compiled token therefore passes the sum-elimination graphical test. Finite distributivity gives the exact successor identity
\[
 K'=\sum_{Z_\zeta}\prod_{k\in L}K_k.
\tag{11}
\]
Cross-multiplication after putting the finitely many rational factors over their registered common denominator proves the polynomial obligation. The successor removes the nonempty set \(Z_\zeta\) from the current random mask, so its first measure coordinate is strictly smaller.

Suppose next that (10) fails and \(|\mathsf D(\zeta)|>1\). Districts are the equivalence classes of bidirected connectivity and hence are explicitly computable and form a disjoint partition
\[
 R_\zeta=D_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}D_j,
 \qquad j\ge 2,
 \qquad D_i\subsetneq R_\zeta.
\tag{12}
\]
The finite topological quotient of the predecessor kernel supplies the canonically ordered district factors. Multiplying those factors and cancelling only common numerator--denominator factors recovers the predecessor kernel; cross-multiplication is therefore an exact polynomial identity. Each child task is queried on all of \(D_i\), so it has no local nonancestor to remove, and its induced graph has the single district \(D_i\). Thus refreshing immediately after the split creates no replacement district token at the same random mask. The split consumes the sole \(\ell\)-token. Since the elimination coordinate precedes the fixing coordinate in \(\mu_H\), any fixing work exposed inside the child tasks occurs only in a later coordinate, and \(\mu_H\) decreases.

It remains to justify that a graphically reachable fixing is never blocked by an assumed certificate. Maintain the following invariant for each branch-reachable, structurally nonzero current kernel cell: it has a reduced representation
\[
 K_k=\frac{N_k}{D_k},
\tag{13}
\]
where \(D_k\) is a product of already registered positive entries and \(N_k\) is a finite positive-expression tree whose leaves are positive supported context cells and whose internal nodes are nonempty sums or products. At initialization, (13) follows from (9), with numerator \(q(v,s)>0\). Selector substitution only removes structurally impossible leaves and preserves (13) on the admissible cells. A finite sum or product combines the corresponding positive-expression trees. A preceding fixing or topological quotient appends its already verified positive divisor to \(D_k\). This proves (13) inductively for every current kernel.

For the least \(W\) satisfying (7), put the finitely many summands in
\[
 m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}
\tag{14}
\]
over the common denominator \(D=\prod_{x_W}D_{x_W}\). Equations (13)--(14) give
\[
 m_{s,W}
 =\frac{
 \sum_{x_W}N_{x_W}\prod_{x'_W\ne x_W}D_{x'_W}}
 {\prod_{x_W}D_{x_W}}.
\tag{15}
\]
At least one summand is structurally admissible because a kernel is normalized on its finite alphabet. The numerator of (15) is consequently a nonempty sum of products of positive certified leaves, and its denominator is a product of earlier positive entries. The compiler constructs the tree in (15), expands both sides, and checks the identity coefficient by coefficient; it does not assume positivity. The frozen lemma \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\) then implies \(m_{s,W}>0\) at every compatible observed law. Together with (7), this is precisely the required eligibility certificate for \(\textnormal{def:fixing-transition}\). Fixing removes \(W\) from the current random mask, so the first coordinate of \(\mu_H\) decreases.

For completeness, the positive-expression certificate in (15) has the stricter supported-margin form required by the fixing transition. The current kernel was obtained from an initialized supported-context kernel by a recorded valid fixing sequence and district restrictions. Since (7) makes \(W\) fixable, append \(W\) to that valid sequence and use \(\textnormal{lem:fixing-order-invariance}\) to move it to the next canonical position. In the resulting topological quotient, (14) is a conditional margin of the original context kernel, hence has the form
\[
 m_{s,W}
 =\frac{
 \sum_{v\in B_1}p_H(v,s)}
 {\prod_{j\in J}d_{H,j}},
 \qquad
 B_1\neq\varnothing,
\tag{15a}
\]
after cancellation, where \(B_1\) contains only cells compatible with the branch assignments and every \(d_{H,j}\) was registered earlier. This representation follows inductively from the topological quotient: marginalizing the next fixable variable replaces the current numerator by a marginal sum, while division appends its previously constructed conditional normalizer to the denominator registry. Equality of (15) and (15a) is checked by the same finite cross-multiplication. Thus the new numerator is a nonempty sum of supported admissible-cell probabilities and the inherited divisor is a product of earlier ledger entries; no broader positivity assertion is smuggled into eligibility.

If none of the four predicates holds, the displayed conjunction in \(\textnormal{def:initial-token-compiler}\) holds and, by definition, the state is residual-ready. Thus every nonresidual refreshed state has the asserted eligible successor and every such successor has smaller \(\mu_H\). A nonterminal stop before residual readiness is impossible.

added_lemmas.statement: Fix a successful run of Algorithms~1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser that uses only selector contexts in \(H\) and only denominators supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\). Order its finite derivation DAG dependency-topologically, breaking ties by the published topological vertex order and then by the context order inherited from \(\operatorname{enc}_H\). The fixed input-determined recursion generated by \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\) simulates this ordered derivation without entering a residual state early. After \(k\) scheduled operations, gate reinsertion makes every emitted labelled kernel equal to its published counterpart modulo the retained image equations, every registered denominator is the corresponding supported positive margin, and the refreshed agenda is exactly the unexecuted suffix of the canonical derivation. At the successful terminal call, the accumulated published functional occurs as the canonical projection candidate and passes the residual polynomial verifier.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(\tau=(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_m)\) be the stated dependency-topological ordering. This order is not supplied to the machine; it is used only to state the simulation invariant. The machine receives the normalized state and the fixed orders encoded by \(\operatorname{enc}_H\).

At \(k=0\), the context-labelled input kernel for every used context \(s\in H\) is
\[
 q_s(v)=p_H(V=v\mid S=s)
 =\frac{p_H(v,s)}
 {
 \sum_{v':(v',s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v',s)
 }.
\tag{16}
\]
This is the same conditional kernel used by the published run. Its denominator is positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\), and \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) says that gate reinsertion maps the normalized primitive coordinates and both maps evaluated from them back to the original expansion. Thus the invariant holds before the first operation.

Assume it holds after \(k<m\) operations. Because the current labelled kernels agree modulo \(\mathcal J\), their current CADMG masks, supported context labels, ancestor sets, districts, and reachability predicates agree. The compiler and the published recursion therefore inspect identical finite predicates. We compare the possible next operations.

If a selector multiplexer occurrence remains, both calculations evaluate the known gate at its supported context. The stored gate equation gives (8), so the two successor kernels are equal and no new denominator is introduced. If no gate remains and a local nonancestor set is nonempty, both calculations apply the same finite marginalization (11). If the current task has several districts, both apply the same topologically ordered proper-district quotient. If a reachable fixing is required, both divide by the conditional margin (14). A published valid fixing order need not begin with the compiler's least valid vertex, but \(\textnormal{lem:fixing-order-invariance}\) makes the resulting kernel independent of that valid ordering. Hence the least choice cannot divert a successful recursion.

In the fixing case, (15) constructs the margin certificate from already registered positive kernels. Because the present theorem assumes that the published denominator is supported, all of its terminal leaves occur among the admissible cells in (16). The frozen denominator-positivity lemma therefore proves that the registered divisor is positive on \(O_H(\Theta_H)\). In every case, expanding finite sums and products and cross-multiplying by the registered positive divisors proves that the new normalized circuit equals the published circuit modulo \(\mathcal J\).

This comparison also covers the three successful district cases of the published algorithms, rather than only ordinary ID. If the published closure of a requested district \(D^*\) equals \(D^*\), its output is a valid fixing of a laid-back supported context kernel, which is the fixing case above. If \(D^*\subsetneq\operatorname{cl}(D^*)\) and the selector is outside the closure, the successful published test supplies a context \(s\in H\) in which \(D^*\) is reachable; the compiler's finite context test selects the least such label and fixing-order invariance gives the same kernel. If the selector belongs to the closure, success of published Algorithm~2 supplies a context \(\bar s\in H\), a district \(D'\supseteq D^*\), the stated graphical separation, and reachability of \(D^*\) in the context graph. The selector transition performs the serious-value substitutions, the labelled district transition forms the ordered product over selector descendants and nondescendants, and the fixing transition applies \(\phi_{D'\setminus D^*}\). These are exactly the factors in the published hybrid kernel. A context failing the separation or reachability test emits no token in either recursion; the fixed context tie-breaker selects the first passing context. Thus no successful published district case is omitted by the four transition relations.

The case priority cannot produce a premature residual. Indeed, residual readiness is the simultaneous failure of the four graphical predicates. If the next published operation is a gate evaluation, ancestor restriction, district split, or reachable fixing, the corresponding predicate is true and \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\) schedules it. Conversely, if an earlier compiler predicate is true, the standard recursive identities permit that operation before the published next operation: marginalization of nonancestors and district multiplication concern disjoint recursive tasks, while a different valid fixing order yields the same kernel by fixing-order invariance. Reordering the finite derivation DAG by these commuting dependencies and the fixed tie-breakers therefore places the compiler's operation next. Removing this operation leaves precisely the dependency-topological unexecuted suffix. This closes the induction.

After \(m\) operations, the accumulated circuit \(C_\tau\) is the functional returned by the published run, with the same supported context normalizers and fixing margins. By construction of \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\), \(C_\tau\) is the first canonical projection in the residual token. The induction supplies at each step an exact cross-multiplied identity; composing those identities yields
\[
 D_\tau\,t_{a,H}^N-P_\tau(o_H^N)=0\pmod{\mathcal J},
\tag{17}
\]
where \(C_\tau=P_\tau/D_\tau\) after cancellation and every factor of \(D_\tau\) is in the positivity ledger. Thus the projection candidate passes the residual verifier. The cited soundness theorem for Algorithm~1 identifies its terminal circuit with the causal query, while (17) gives the stronger algebraic equality needed by the present verifier. This proves all three components of the simulation invariant and the terminal acceptance claim.

proposed.name: priorityH
proposed.def: After refreshing the agenda with \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\), \(\mathfrak P_H\) selects, in order: an actually present selector-correction token; the nonancestor sum-elimination token; the proper-district elimination token; the canonically least reachable-fixing token; or the sole residual token. Within a case it uses the order from \(\operatorname{enc}_H\). No unnamed transition or unsupplied context is eligible.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen priority selected fixing before ancestor removal and district splitting, contrary to the required input-determined recursive case order.

proposed_core_edits.name: muH

proposed.name: muH
proposed.def: \(\mu_H(\zeta)=(|R|,|\Sigma|,|\mathcal L|,|\mathcal F|,|\mathcal R|)\), ordered lexicographically after compiler refresh. A selector transition reduces \(|\Sigma|\); a nonancestor elimination or fixing transition reduces \(|R|\); a district split consumes its sole current \(\ell\)-token before any newly exposed fixing work; and a residual transition consumes the sole residual token and halts.

proposed_core_edits.reason: With a regenerated agenda, district splitting may expose fixing work. Placing fixing-token count before elimination-token count can therefore increase the old lexicographic measure. Swapping those two coordinates makes selector discharge, vertex removal, and district-token consumption decrease in the compiler's case order.

proposed.name: current-state recursive agenda compiler
proposed.construction:
For a nonterminal encoded state \(\zeta\), let the current task be the lexicographically least unfinished labelled kernel block under \(\operatorname{enc}_H\), and let \(G_\zeta\), \(R_\zeta\), and \(Y_\zeta\) denote its current CADMG, random mask, and local outcome mask. The deterministic compiler \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\) refreshes the agenda from the current state, rather than from a proposed derivation, as follows.

First form \(\mathsf G(\zeta)\), the lexicographically ordered list of all occurrences of stored selector multiplexers that are actually present in a current context-labelled kernel with context in \(H\). If \(\mathsf G(\zeta)\neq\varnothing\), set \(\Sigma=\mathsf G(\zeta)\) and set the other newly generated agenda lists to empty. Once \(\mathsf G(\zeta)=\varnothing\), assign each unfinished recursive district task the lexicographically least context in \(H\) satisfying its displayed laid-back or override values, graphical separation test, and reachability test, if such a context exists; otherwise retain its target-only-hole label. These are finite tests on the current stored graphs and kernels, and a failing context test creates no token. Select the least unfinished task, and define its fixing set to be empty when it has only a hole label. Apply the following mutually exclusive case list in the displayed order:
\[
 Z_\zeta=R_\zeta\setminus\operatorname{an}_{G_\zeta}(Y_\zeta),
 \qquad
 \mathsf D(\zeta)=\operatorname{dis}(G_\zeta),
 \qquad
 \mathsf W(\zeta)=
 \left\{W\in R_\zeta:
 \operatorname{dis}_{G_\zeta}(W)\cap
 \operatorname{de}_{G_\zeta}(W)=\{W\}
 \right\}.
\]
If \(Z_\zeta\neq\varnothing\), generate exactly the sum-elimination token for \(Z_\zeta\). Otherwise, if \(|\mathsf D(\zeta)|>1\), generate exactly the district-elimination token whose child tasks are the districts in encoded order, each queried on all of its vertices. Otherwise, if \(\mathsf W(\zeta)\neq\varnothing\), generate exactly the fixing token for the least element of \(\mathsf W(\zeta)\). Its margin certificate is computed, not postulated: put the finitely many current rational kernel cells over the common product of previously registered denominators, expand the finite sum over the alphabet of \(W\), recursively label every leaf by either a supported positive context cell or an earlier positive-ledger entry, cancel common factors, and verify the resulting polynomial identity by cross-multiplication. If all four predicates fail, declare the state residual-ready and generate the sole residual token. Its projection list starts with the canonical composite of the labelled sum, product, district, and fixing circuits already stored in the state and then lists the remaining circuits generated by the fixed labelled elimination order; its contrast list is the encoded signed-row-swap list. Thus residual-ready means
\[
 \mathsf G(\zeta)=\varnothing,
 \qquad Z_\zeta=\varnothing,
 \qquad |\mathsf D(\zeta)|=1,
 \qquad \mathsf W(\zeta)=\varnothing,
\]
independently of whether any residual candidate passes its verifier. All context, vertex, district, and circuit ties are broken by \(\operatorname{enc}_H\). After every admitted transition the compiler is rerun on the successor. No token that fails its current graphical predicate is placed on the refreshed agenda.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the required sole input-determined compiler. It defines initial and regenerated agendas by explicit decidable graphical predicates and constructs, rather than assumes, fixing-margin certificates.

proposed.name: executable SA-CS-ID transition system
proposed.construction:
Initialize, for every \(s\in H\), the labelled context kernel
\[
 K_s(v)=\frac{p_H(v,s)}{\sum_{v':(v',s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v',s)},
\]
the retained constraint list from \(\mathcal I_H\), and the unfinished root task. Apply \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\) to obtain the initial agenda. At each nonterminal state rerun \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\) after the preceding successor has been formed, and apply the unique case selected by \(\mathfrak P_H\): a selector correction if an actual supported-context gate occurrence remains; otherwise removal of the nonempty nonancestor set; otherwise proper-district splitting; otherwise the canonically least reachable fixing whose ledger certificate is produced by the recursive positive-expression construction; otherwise residual compilation. The selected transition is admitted only after its finite graphical eligibility test, exact cross-multiplied polynomial identity, and every required positivity-ledger identity have succeeded. The successor must have smaller \(\mu_H\). The residual relation is the only halting relation and emits either a verifier-accepted rational circuit with its complete denominator domain or a verifier-accepted global-twin box. The compiler depends only on the current normalized state and the fixed input order; neither a published derivation nor a successful agenda is an input.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The machine must invoke the sole current-state compiler initially and after every successor, use the required case priority, and never accept a preloaded ineligible token or a published derivation as input.

proposed.statement: Each eligible selector-correction, reachable-fixing, labelled-elimination, and residual-compilation transition preserves the represented observation-target relation on its registered branch domain after composing its emitted circuit, and discharges exactly its displayed polynomial identity or inequality obligation. For every nonhalting transition \(\zeta\Rightarrow\zeta'\), \(\mu_H(\zeta')<_{\mathrm{lex}}\mu_H(\zeta)\): selector correction removes one \(\sigma\)-token, fixing removes one active vertex, elimination removes a nonempty active set or one \(\ell\)-token, and residual compilation removes the sole residual token and enters a terminal state. Therefore the deterministic schedule terminates after finitely many encoded transitions, conditional only on the residual verifier finding a candidate.
proposed.justification: The calculus is executable only when every scheduled move has a decidable eligibility test, an exact successor, a local invariant, and an input-determined progress rule.
proposed.gap: The anchor algorithm names graphical operations but does not provide a fixed-support retained-image transition semantics with a regenerated agenda and per-rule decreasing certificate.
proposed.consumer: A selector-aware implementation can construct its next agenda from the logged state, reject malformed transitions, and replay every certificate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The established local soundness proof must consume the new nonresidual progress lemma, and its termination claim must be read with the corrected regenerated-agenda measure.

proposed.statement: Whenever Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser return an identifying functional using only selector values in \(H\) and denominators supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})\), \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\) returns \((F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\) such that \(O_H(\theta)\in\mathfrak D_H\) and \(F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\). Gate reinsertion makes the returned circuit and its required positive margins algebraically equal to the published derivation on the original expansion.
proposed.justification: The proved fixed-recursion simulation shows that every support-licensed positive formula of the anchor algorithm is retained without making that successful derivation part of the machine input.
proposed.gap: This closes positive-branch preservation through fixed-support normalization; it does not settle the anchor algorithm's unresolved failure branch or the present all-residual dichotomy.
proposed.consumer: Existing systematic-selection analyses obtain the same estimand and can adopt the normalized backend without changing a valid reported formula or silently adding a context.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The preservation theorem now depends explicitly on the fixed compiler and the proved published-trace simulation, eliminating the prior circular use of a successful derivation as an agenda.

proposed.comparator_claim: Algorithms 1--2 return sound identifying formulas on successful branches.
The systematic-selection algorithm is conjectured to be complete beyond its specified failure branches.
Ordinary semi-Markovian ID is complete through identifying formulas or hedge countermodels.
Positive gID is sound and complete by reduction to classical ID subproblems.
Root-control CSI identification is equivalent to finitely many ordinary graphical identification problems.
Finite canonical SCMs represent all categorical counterfactual distributions and yield sharp polynomial-program bounds.
The arithmetic-circuit method is at least as complete as classical ID and do-calculus under strict positivity and can exploit additional model constraints.
Sufficient pruning and transit-clustering conditions preserve identification conclusions and transport do-calculus functionals.
Influence-function and weight-based estimators are derived for broad classes of identified effects in hidden-variable graphical models.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The honest post-repair positioning proves only positive-trace preservation; the all-residual completion and the strengthened ordinary hedge equivalence remain open, so the old table's headline matches were stale.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that every residual-ready normalized state contains either a verifier-accepted rational projection identity or a verifier-accepted common signed-row contrast, and rule out an identified residual whose induced observable functional is algebraic but nonrational.
open_obligations.obstruction: The fixed compiler and progress proof now force every run to a residual-ready state, but none of the frozen assumptions makes the finite projection and contrast libraries exhaustive over interacting districts. General semialgebraic fiber constancy does not imply membership in the rational circuit library, while a local row swap need not preserve all supported observed descendants.
open_obligations.attempted: The Lee-Ghassami-Shpitser ancestor, district, and fixing recursion closes every nonresidual state and compiles all successful positive traces. On the negative side, ordinary hedge and general-identifiability witnesses were tested against the certificate contract; their published constructions do not by themselves provide an arbitrary-finite-alphabet rational-affine box, strict supported-cell positivity, exact selector support, and polynomial equality of every supported cell after lifting through descendants.
open_obligations.partial_result:
With the input-determined compiler installed, \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\) makes every nonresidual transition strictly decrease \(\mu_H\in\mathbb N^5\). Lexicographic order on \(\mathbb N^5\) is well founded, so every execution reaches a residual-ready state after finitely many nonresidual transitions. If its verifier accepts a formula, then \(\textnormal{thm:certificate-soundness}\) gives
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H,
 \qquad
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta),
\]
so the target is constant on observation fibers. If it accepts a twin box, the same theorem supplies \(\theta_b^+,\theta_b^-\in\Theta_H\) with equal observations, unequal targets, exact support \(H\), and positive admissible cells, so identification fails. Determinism gives at most one certificate. What remains is existence of an accepted residual candidate and the converse excluding an identified but nonrational residual.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Compile every ordinary ID hedge into the exact residual contrast representation required by the frozen verifier.
open_obligations.obstruction: Classical ID completeness supplies a hedge witness but the present negative certificate is stronger: it requires fixed canonical response tables, independent-root factorization, rational-affine dependence on one open rational box, strict positivity of every admissible observed cell, exact support, and an encoded coefficient-bound sign certificate. A common-baseline mixture is not automatically legal because coordinatewise mixing through a polynomial SCM can destroy observed-law equality.
open_obligations.attempted: The structural normalization and every nonresidual ID operation were reduced exactly, and successful ordinary formulas are projection candidates. The hedge route was not declared proved because no induction was obtained that simultaneously preserves the full observed law through arbitrary observed descendants and keeps a nonzero target contrast under the required positive rational perturbation.
open_obligations.partial_result: When \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), exact support gives \(p_\theta(S=s_{\emptyset})=1\). Every gate is laid back, and absence of a latent root shared by \(S\) and \(V\) permits deletion of the constant selector coordinate without changing any substantive root factorization. Hence \(G_H^N\) is the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion, \(p_\theta(v,s_{\emptyset})=p_\theta(v)\), and normalization equivalence identifies \(\Phi_H\) with the ordinary observational-target relation. The compiler's nonresidual ancestor, district, and fixing operations are then exactly the ordinary ID operations. A successful ordinary ID formula is encoded by the projection side of \(\textnormal{lem:published-trace-scheduling}\). The unproved part is the failing side: a hedge must still be compiled into the verifier's rational-affine, strictly positive, arbitrary-finite-alphabet global-twin box.

prose_updates.tldr: For a finite selector-gated semi-Markovian SCM observed on exactly \(H\), the independently constructed retained carrier is equivalent to the original parameterization. The repaired SA-CS-ID machine now has one compiler determined solely by the current normalized state: it enumerates actual supported gate occurrences and then applies the fixed nonancestor, district, and reachable-fixing case order, constructing its positivity certificates inductively. Nonresidual progress and simulation of every support-licensed successful Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser trace are proved, so published positive formulas are preserved without installing the successful trace as an agenda. Certificate soundness and finite progress reduce the remaining headline to the explicit all-residual rational-projection-or-global-twin question. That residual exhaustiveness result, including exclusion of identified nonrational residuals, and the strengthened positive-box compiler for ordinary hedges remain open.

project_justification.fill: The project constructs the intrinsic normalized carrier \(\Lambda_H\), proves its constrained subset \(\mathcal I_H\) equals the original fixed-support image, and defines an input-determined four-relation machine with exact local algebraic obligations and a denominator positivity ledger. The present repair proves exhaustive nonresidual progress and preservation of all support-licensed successful published derivations. A complete field-level result still requires the residual theorem: every residual-ready state must yield either a verified rational identifying circuit on the full compatible image or a support-exact global-twin box.

prose_updates.related_work: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024) provide the selector-gated model, Algorithms 1--2, soundness in Theorem 4, branchwise witnesses in Theorem 5, and an explicit completeness conjecture. The fixed compiler proved here simulates every successful support-licensed positive run, but their failure results do not supply the exact-support, restricted-interior global twins required for the residual converse. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) provide ordinary ID formula-or-hedge completeness; translating an arbitrary categorical hedge into this machine's rational-affine positive-box certificate remains an additional obligation rather than an imported conclusion. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022) motivate general-identifiability witnesses, but their constructions do not directly establish a common contrast preserving one selector-coupled joint law on exactly \(H\). Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022) provide finite canonical response types, not exhaustiveness of the present rational projection and signed-row-swap libraries. Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen (2026) give sufficient graph reductions and formula transport for general data fusion, not inverse fixed-support parameter maps or all-branch twins. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2021) supply the dosearch software consumer.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The input-determined compiler removes the prior possibility of a nonresidual stuck state and the published-trace simulation settles positive preservation. It does not prove that a residual projection or signed-row contrast passes. In an interacting-district residual, fiber constancy could in principle induce an algebraic but nonrational functional, and a local contrast can be annihilated or exposed by observed descendants. The ordinary special case also still lacks the verifier-level arbitrary-alphabet, strictly positive rational-box compilation of a hedge. Boundary-uniform inference, off-domain regularization, and unrestricted quantifier elimination remain outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established are retained-image normalization, local transition soundness, restricted-support denominator positivity, an explicit current-state agenda compiler, exhaustive nonresidual progress, and operation-by-operation preservation of support-licensed successful Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser formulas. The all-residual formula-or-global-twin dichotomy is still to be proved, including rationality on every identified residual and a common support-preserving contrast on every nonidentified residual. For \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), the graph, observed-target relation, and nonresidual recursion reduce to ordinary ID, while the stronger rational-affine positive-box encoding of every hedge remains open. No context outside \(H\) is supplied, no uniform positivity constant is assumed, and no completeness conclusion is claimed from generic semialgebraic elimination.
